clue.text: Soft pulp with space to grow rapidly

parts.note: mush is a soft, pulpy mass
room means space, as in room to move

explanation.surface: Advice on letting something soft and pulpy expand quickly with enough room.
explanation.definitionFit: To mushroom is to spread or increase suddenly, as the fungi spring up overnight.

clue.text: In ignorance of universal directions to contain a conflict

parts.note: U is the film-classification abbreviation for universal

indicators.note: to contain means the compass letters hold the next pieces between them

parts.note: N and E, north and east, are two compass directions
a war is a conflict

explanation.surface: Someone oblivious to orders that all sides should keep a fight in check.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to contain' puts A WAR between the two directions N and E, after U.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unaware of something is being ignorant of it, a phrase with the same preposition-taking use.

clue.text: So strong, he can rule freely

indicators.note: freely suggests the letters of these three words move about without restraint into a new order

explanation.surface: A man so powerful that he can govern without constraint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'freely' rearranges the letters of HE CAN RULE.
explanation.definitionFit: Herculean means of immense strength, like the mythical hero Hercules.

clue.text: Former pupil with lanky figure

parts.note: OB, old boy, is a former pupil of a school
lanky means long and thin

explanation.surface: An old schoolboy with a tall, gangly build.
explanation.walkthrough: 'figure' looks like a body shape but means a geometric shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A rectangle longer than it is wide is a geometric shape of that name.

clue.text: Stoneworker's mother, great at first with child

definitions.note: read as 'stoneworker is', the 's being a link

indicators.note: at first tells us the word for great is placed before the other pieces

parts.note: monumental means great in size or importance
ma is an informal word for mother
a son is a child

explanation.surface: A craftsman's mother, heavily pregnant at the start, with her baby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' tells you the word for great leads, though the clue mentions it after mother; 'great' is not a description of the pregnant mother.
explanation.definitionFit: A monumental mason carves gravestones and memorials, a trade of working with stone.

clue.text: A youngster embraced her — an innocent child

indicators.note: embraced means the word for youngster holds the next word inside it

parts.note: a cub is a young animal, or a young person in the Scouts
taken as written

explanation.surface: A little one hugged its mother, a picture of childlike innocence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embraced' signals a container; 'A youngster' is one piece, the article included.
explanation.definitionFit: A cherub is an angel painted as a chubby, innocent infant, so it is used for a sweet child.

clue.text: Quartet participating in sensual festivities

indicators.note: participating in means the four is placed within the word for sensual

parts.note: carnal means of the flesh, sensual
IV is four in Roman numerals, a quartet being a group of four

explanation.surface: Four people joining in some rather fleshly revelry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'participating in' signals a container; Quartet suggests musicians but is just the Roman numeral for four.
explanation.definitionFit: A carnival is a public celebration with processions and merrymaking.

clue.text: Half-cooked morsel of food

parts.note: rare meat is only lightly cooked
a bit is a small piece or morsel

explanation.surface: A small bite of something not fully cooked.
explanation.walkthrough: RAREBIT, often Welsh rarebit, is cheese on toast.
explanation.definitionFit: Rarebit is a dish of melted cheese on toast, a savoury snack.

clue.text: Two fellows take in many belonging to a church

parts.note: Basil is a man's name

indicators.note: take in means the second name holds the next letter inside it

parts.note: Ian is a second man's name
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, hence many

explanation.surface: A couple of men welcome a crowd into their congregation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take in' signals a container acting on the second name only; many is the Roman hundred.
explanation.definitionFit: Basilican is the adjective from basilica, a large early or privileged church.

clue.text: Exactly right character to be detailed for reconnaissance

parts.note: pat, as in off pat, means exactly right or perfectly learnt

indicators.note: detailed is read as de-tailed, the word losing its tail or last letter

parts.note: a role is a character played by an actor

explanation.surface: Precisely the right person to be assigned to scouting duty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be detailed' looks like 'assigned' but means cutting the last letter E off ROLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A patrol is a group sent out to watch or scout an area, a reconnaissance mission.

clue.text: Trains make scheduled trip back, taking in the old town

indicators.note: taking in means the reversed letters hold the ancient city within them
back means the words for scheduled and trip are read in reverse

parts.note: set means fixed or scheduled, as in a set time
a run is a short trip
Ur is the ancient Mesopotamian city

explanation.surface: Railway services complete their return journeys via an ancient settlement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the two words into NURTES; 'taking in' adds the ancient city inside. 'Trains' is the verb, not railway carriages.
explanation.definitionFit: To nurture is to rear and educate, so trains is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Poisonous tree? The French incinerate them, some say

indicators.note: some say means the phrase is spoken to give the sound of the answer

parts.note: la is French for the, burn means incinerate, and 'em is them

explanation.surface: A question about a toxic tree, and the French habit of burning such trees.
explanation.walkthrough: LA BURN 'EM, spoken, gives the tree's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The laburnum has yellow hanging flowers and seeds that are toxic, making it a poisonous species.

clue.text: Is third man a yellowish-grey colour?

parts.note: Abel, son of Adam and Eve, was the third man in the Bible after Adam and Cain

explanation.surface: A question whether some third person is a drab shade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'third man' suggests the film The Third Man, but means Abel.
explanation.definitionFit: Isabel, or isabelline, is a greyish-yellow shade, traditionally said of horses.

clue.text: 50% hire-purchase? By no means

indicators.note: fifty per cent means only half of the phrase is kept

parts.note: the ...-... is British slang for buying on hire purchase

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to pay half on credit.
explanation.walkthrough: The never-never is British slang for hire purchase, buying in instalments; keep half of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Never means at no time, not at all, an emphatic refusal.

clue.text: On which many press stories have appeared

definitions.text: On which many press stories have appeared

parts.words: On which many press stories have appeared
parts.note: reads as a place with a history of media coverage but literally describes the cheap paper newspapers are printed on

explanation.definitionFit: Newspapers are printed on this cheap paper, so their stories literally appear on it.

clue.text: A new device about right for an icy area

indicators.note: about means the word for device goes around the letter for right

parts.note: a tactic is a device or ploy

explanation.surface: A fresh gadget to cope with frozen terrain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts R inside TACTIC, after A and N.
explanation.definitionFit: The Antarctic is the frozen region round the South Pole.

clue.text: Bird, fish or insect

parts.note: a cock is a male bird
a roach is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A quiz-style choice between three kinds of creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' looks like a list of alternatives; it is a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A cockroach is a scavenging insect.

clue.text: Instrument for effecting change in spy organization?

indicators.note: in means the word for change goes inside the rearranged letters
organization signals the letters of spy are reorganized

parts.note: to alter is to effect a change

explanation.surface: Asking what tool might reform a spy ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organization' rearranges the spy into PSY; 'in' signals the container. Spy organization looks like an agency.
explanation.definitionFit: A psaltery is an ancient stringed instrument, plucked like a zither.

clue.text: Starting time for Grundy's joint venture

definitions.text: Starting time for Grundy's joint venture

parts.words: Starting time for Grundy's joint venture
parts.note: a business launch in surface, but recalls the nursery rhyme of Solomon Grundy, who was married on this day

explanation.surface: When a business partnership began.
explanation.walkthrough: In the nursery rhyme Solomon Grundy is born on Monday, christened on Tuesday and married on Wednesday; marriage is the 'joint venture'.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhyme gives this weekday as the day of Solomon Grundy's wedding, the start of his married life.

clue.text: Parts of old England and Wales, perhaps? Not entirely

indicators.note: perhaps signals that the letters could be arranged another way
not entirely means the word is cut short by its final letter

explanation.surface: Areas of historic England and possibly Wales, though not wholly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not entirely' trims Wales to WALE; 'perhaps' rearranges AND WALE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Danelaw was the region of England under Danish rule in Viking times.

clue.text: A once-calamitous waste of water

indicators.note: calamitous suggests disaster, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A former disaster of a watery wilderness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'calamitous' rearranges A ONCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ocean is a vast expanse of sea, the poetic 'waste of waters'.

clue.text: Counsellor reads novel about Virgin Islands

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go around the islands abbreviation
novel means new, so these letters take a new order

explanation.surface: A therapist reading fiction set in the Caribbean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' makes ADSER from the letters read; 'about' wraps that around the islands. Novel looks like a book being read.
explanation.definitionFit: An adviser gives guidance, just as a counsellor does.

clue.text: He picks off birds on the river

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed above the following letter

parts.note: snipe, plural as singular, are wading birds

explanation.surface: A hunter shoots waterfowl by the riverside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He picks off birds' looks like the whole definition; only 'He picks off' is.
explanation.definitionFit: A sniper shoots individual targets from cover, one at a time.

clue.text: Producer of writing page one in enclosure

indicators.note: in means the numeral sits inside the abbreviation for enclosure

parts.note: encl. is the abbreviation for enclosure on a letter
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A note about where the writer slipped page one into an envelope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enclosure' tempts PEN, but it is ENCL; 'in' puts I inside it after P.
explanation.definitionFit: A pencil is an instrument for making marks on paper.

clue.text: Male lexicographer with roots in South America

parts.note: a man is a male
Sir George Grove compiled the Grove Dictionary of Music

explanation.surface: A man who writes dictionaries and was born in South America.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the tree's stilt roots in tropical swamps and on its name, taken from a Caribbean Taino word via Spanish and Portuguese.
explanation.definitionFit: These tropical trees grow with tangled aerial roots in tidal swamps along South American coasts.

clue.text: Pansy's love in such a useless state?

definitions.text: Pansy's love in such a useless state?

parts.words: Pansy's love in such a useless state?
parts.note: reads as a girl named Pansy lovelorn and listless, but recalls the flower's old name love-in-a-state-of-inaction

explanation.surface: A woman called Pansy is lovesick and lethargic.
explanation.walkthrough: An old name for the wild pansy is love-in-idleness, from Shakespeare's Midsummer Night's Dream.
explanation.definitionFit: Idleness is a state of inactivity or uselessness, the 'useless state' named in the flower's old name.

clue.text: Leading artist is first to earn commendation

parts.note: PRA is President of the Royal Academy, the leading artist in Britain

indicators.note: first to means only the opening letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: A top painter is the first to win acclaim.
explanation.walkthrough: PRA, President of the Royal Academy, is a crossword convention for a top artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Praise is approval expressed, much as a commendation is.

clue.text: Inferior army transport outside the War Department …

indicators.note: outside means the army and transport letters go around the department abbreviation

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a means of transport
WD is the abbreviation for the War Department

explanation.surface: Second-rate military vehicles parked beyond a government ministry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' signals the container; the dots join this to the next clue only for the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Tawdry means cheap and showy, of poor quality.

clue.text: … and not the service for this underground line?

parts.note: nor means and not
RN, the Royal Navy, is one of the armed services

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: not the forces' route on the Tube.
explanation.walkthrough: The Northern line is one of London's Underground lines.
explanation.definitionFit: The Northern line is a route on the London Underground railway network.
